steps.name: Audit
steps.title: Step 1.1 Audit: nine tasks, eight tied to an outside source

tasks.name: Website
tasks.text: Speed and usability for real visitors, measured at the 75th percentile of page loads.

tasks.name: Search
tasks.text: Whether Google can index and show the pages, and any manual actions against the site.

tasks.name: Tracking
tasks.text: Whether the tags work, using each platform's own diagnostic tool. Meta's tool also flags duplicated Pixel code.

tasks.name: Consent and notice
tasks.text: Whether visitors' consent choices are passed on, and whether the site gives the notice Meta's terms require.

tasks.name: Data link
tasks.text: Whether sale results reach the ad platforms, by which route, and how well they match.

tasks.name: Ad accounts
tasks.text: Each platform's own account score and recommendations. Meta delivers its best-practice guidance through its opportunity score.

tasks.name: Attribution
tasks.text: Which rule assigns credit for a sale, and the attribution windows in use.

tasks.name: Sales match
tasks.text: Leads matched to the client's sales records by written rules.
tasks.note: No outside source. Experts to confirm.

rules: Every percentage states the group counted, the date range and the rule.

all_phases.title: Regulated industries: five extra steps
all_phases.heading: REGULATED INDUSTRIES: EXTRA STEPS
steps: Bring in a privacy or sector specialist.
Apply each platform's special category settings.
Send no health or financial data to ad platforms.
Have a lawyer review before launch.
notes: Google
restricts targeting for housing, employment and consumer finance in the United States and Canada. Health is a separate sensitive category.
Meta

prohibits discriminatory targeting, sets rules for financial, insurance and health ads, and requires a Special Ad Category for housing, employment, and financial products and services. For advertisers based in or reaching the US, or reaching Canada and certain European countries, that limits targeting by age, gender and ZIP code.
TikTok
has a housing, employment and credit policy for advertisers based in the US or targeting the US or Canada.
FTC
took action against GoodRx and BetterHelp for sharing health data with ad platforms.
sources: Meta: Financial and Insurance Products and Services
Meta: choose a Special Ad Category
TikTok: Housing, Employment and Credit ad policy
all_phases.footnote: Not legal advice. The five extra steps are AugMind's choice. A lawyer has not reviewed them. The FTC actions concern health data only.
